activities.instruction: Read the passage on printed page 7 and choose the best answer.

items.question: Why did the narrator come to the station?
items.explanation: The narrator states the purpose was to see his friend off.

items.question: Where was Sajjad going?
items.explanation: Dhaka is the stated destination, not the unnamed departure station.

items.question: Whom was Sajjad going to visit?
items.explanation: The passage identifies his elder sister’s house.

items.question: What was the woman in the queue doing?
items.explanation: The woman in the ticket queue held her child’s hand.

items.question: Why was the old couple looking for a quiet place?
What was the young lady reading?
items.explanation: She was sitting with her luggage and reading a magazine.

items.question: Where did Sajjad and the narrator stand while watching the crowd?
items.explanation: The second paragraph names the newspaper stall.

activities.instruction: Answer from the reading passage. The question about resting allows a supported inference.

items.question: Describe the crowd at the ticket counter.
items.modelAnswer: There was a long line of people at the ticket counter.

items.question: What were the young people near the tea stall doing?
items.modelAnswer: They were talking loudly and drinking tea in front of the stall.

items.question: Why might it have been difficult for the old couple to rest in the waiting room?
items.modelAnswer: The waiting room was crowded too, so it might have been difficult to find a quiet place there.

items.question: What difficulty was one man having with his luggage?
items.modelAnswer: He was trying to carry three heavy suitcases.

items.question: What did Sajjad do as the train whistled?
items.modelAnswer: He picked up his suitcase, and he and the narrator said goodbye to each other.

activities.instruction: Give the requested contextual meaning or opposite.

acceptedAnswers: go with someone to their departure point and say goodbye
a line of people waiting their turn

items.request: give an opposite for lifting an object

activities.note: The textbook matching exercise pairs quiet with busy; these contrast this station context but are not universal antonyms. Put down is a more direct opposite of pick up (lift) than drop. Accept drop where the task explicitly follows the book’s supplied choices.

activities.instruction: Summarise the reading passage in your own words. This seen summary is supplementary skill practice, not the unseen Q7 block of a full model test.
activities.modelAnswer: The narrator visits a crowded railway station to see his friend Sajjad off on a journey to his elder sister’s house in Dhaka. People queue for tickets, drink tea, look for seats and manage their luggage. The friends watch the busy scene near a newspaper stall. When the train whistles and begins to leave, Sajjad picks up his suitcase and they say goodbye.
assessment: Purpose of visit and Sajjad’s destination
Representative details of the crowded station
Concise connected sentences without invented train times or station names

activities.instruction: Look at the picture on printed page 8. Write four sentences describing visible things and actions. Do not assume identities from the separate passage.
activities.modelAnswer: A train is beside a crowded platform. People are standing near the carriage doors. A person is carrying a load on their head. A child is standing beside an adult.
assessment: Does not invent destination, relationships or hidden actions
activities.note: The textbook picture must be available for this task. More than one accurate description is acceptable.

activities.instruction: Imagine that you visited a fair. Describe what you saw, what people were doing and what you did. No fixed word count is imposed for this lesson exercise.
activities.modelAnswer: Last Friday, I visited a book fair with my aunt. We walked slowly past the stalls and looked at colourful covers. Some visitors were comparing prices, while others were asking sellers about new books. A little boy was showing his mother a picture book. We stopped at a stall with stories for young readers. The seller helped me choose a short story collection. My aunt bought a book about birds. After paying, we put the books in our cloth bag and found a quiet place to sit. I read the first page of my new book before we went home. I enjoyed watching people share their interest in reading.
assessment: Suitable past forms and connected sentences
activities.note: Original imagined account based on the A4 writing skill, not an event reported about Sajjad.

limitations: Draft initial pool, not exhaustive quota completion or a full model test.
No departure city, train name, timetable or narrator name is supplied in the passage; none is invented.
No poem in this lesson; no poem tasks added.
